text: After a thoroughly dispiriting 35-6 loss to the Jaguars in Week 3, the Patriots find themselves staring down some uncomfortable questions about their direction, particularly surrounding Drake Maye, whose three turnovers (two interceptions and a lost fumble) in Jacksonville left the rookie quarterback's early-season struggles impossible to ignore—Maye himself called the offensive performance "unacceptable" and acknowledged he needs to look inward for answers as Trevor Lawrence carved up New England's defense with three touchdown passes. The injury situation didn't help matters, with tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) ruled out before the game, while on the brighter side, defensive back Marcus Jones recorded his first interception of the season and second-round linebacker Gabe Jacas continued making an impact on the defensive side of the ball in his early role. With such a lopsided defeat and mounting questions about Maye's development barely three weeks into the season, the Patriots have little time to recalibrate before facing the road ahead.
